- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model should not overreact — cap forecast slope at 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model should not ignore supply constraints — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish signals (e.g., 0.00 or negative) and price is trending up, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model should not assume continuation — apply 1–2% downward correction to later days.  
- If recent auction events are supply-heavy (e.g., multiple DE/CAP3 auctions), model should reduce forecast growth rate by 0.5–1.5% per event to reflect supply pressure.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (e.g., alternating 0.00 and 1.00), model should avoid smooth linear trends — introduce 0.5–1.0% volatility buffer in forecast.
